3.label: 3(a)
3.answer: Physics studies matter, energy and their interactions.
3.explanation: It seeks experimentally tested laws describing physical events.

3.label: 3(b)(i)
3.answer: It helps explain natural events such as rainbows and falling objects.
3.explanation: Optics explains coloured light; gravity explains falling motion.

3.label: 3(b)(ii)
3.answer: It develops measuring and problem-solving skills.
3.explanation: Measurements connect predictions to repeatable evidence.

3.label: 3(b)(iii)
3.answer: It supports technology such as radios, engines and medical imaging.
3.explanation: These devices apply principles of waves, energy and forces.

3.label: 3(b)(iv)
3.answer: It prepares students for careers in engineering, medicine and science.
3.explanation: Those fields use physical models and careful measurements.

9.label: 9(a)(i)
9.answer: Work is energy transferred by a force through displacement; SI unit joule.
9.explanation: For a constant parallel force W=Fs.

9.label: 9(a)(ii)
9.answer: Energy is the capacity to do work; SI unit joule.
9.explanation: Energy can be stored or transferred.

9.label: 9(a)(iii)
9.answer: Power is work done or energy transferred per time; SI unit watt.

10.label: 10(a)(i)
10.answer: Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity.

10.label: 10(a)(ii)
10.answer: Velocity is the rate of change of displacement in a specified direction.

10.label: 10(a)(iii)
10.answer: Speed is distance travelled per unit time.
10.explanation: It has magnitude but no direction.

10.label: 10(a)(iv)
10.answer: Displacement is directed change from initial to final position.
10.explanation: It is a vector measured in metres.
